agree.reason: The warm, specific and modest request makes a counteroffer likely, but nothing tells an editor with a $9,000 cap and an $8,000 newcomer why a $2,500 jump beats switching illustrators.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, and the email rightly leaves out the unsupported claim that every other publisher pays at least $12,000, though calling the books 'done well' and saying 'the market has moved' stretch a little past what one $12,500 fee shows.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts are listed accurately but never worked into figures: there's no per-month rate (about $2,250 over four months), no note that the fee has stayed flat across six books while two sold 20,000+, and no framing of the ask as a single raise after four years.

right_comparison.reason: It compares her fee to the $12,500 outside fee and the agent's range and notes the flat history, but it doesn't make the real comparison for the editor: a proven illustrator whose books sell versus an untested cheaper one.

qualification.reason: A fee request with a clear figure needs no conditional hedge.

objections.reason: The resisting editor's main objection, a fixed $9,000 budget with a cheaper option available, goes unmet; the email could have argued that the sales record justifies the extra cost, but it only touches value through a passing sales mention.

fit.reason: It is a short, properly formatted email of about 210 words, under the 250-word limit, with a clear ask and an offer to talk.
